method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited locator address was checked to begin an instruction of its decoded function, and the operands, name literals, vftable cells, builder calls, constants and call targets named in the claims were compared with those listings by a second pass. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts are call-site and script counts that agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json. Script argument counts and descriptor selectors come from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan that no tracked artifact carries and are INFERRED. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of sixteen DesktopWidget native registrations: _setUserMacroTitle, _getUserMacroTitle, _setUserMacroIcon, _getUserMacroIcon, _setUserMacroData, _getUserMacroData, _saveUserMacro, _setTargetCharacterByDisplayName, _parseTextCommand, _sendCountDown, _waitForItemSearchWidget, _createWidgetInWidgetContainer, _isExistWidgetInWidgetContainer, _isCreatingWidgetInWidgetContainer, _getWidgetFromWidgetContainer and _deleteCreatingWidgetInWidgetContainer. Each row gives the registration site, receiver holder, declared argument and return lists, branches, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish macro file contents, display name values, text command grammar, countdown semantics, widget container contents or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

framework.reference: manifests/achievement_target_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/chara_desktop_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the cell tags, the invalid-parameter route, the return pushers and the world object chain. Each registrar builds the return list first and the argument list second.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the 44 rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. Each switchboard call sits behind a test of the byte at +0x0E of the switchboard argument. The first call of a registrar builds the return list and the second builds the argument list. All sixteen registrars use the wrapper 0x00726BF0.

framework.holdersNote: The invoke routine casts the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor. A null cast returns false without calling the callback.

listBuilders.0x00745380: 13 entries, int, int, Which<Utf8String, int> three times, Utf8String eight times

facts.claim: The callback reads no cell. It reaches W through R, X and Y and calls 0x0075CCD0, which loads V = [W], takes B through 0x004D7540 and calls the writer 0x004C7A80 on B with the force argument 0.

The writer returns at once with al = 1 when the byte at B +0x0D is zero and the force argument is zero. The set natives store 1 there. The writer has no store to B +0x0D, so the dirty byte stays set after a save.

Otherwise the writer loops over 5 groups of 0x14 records with the stride 0x4880 per group and builds a buffer. Each record writes the title as the tag byte at 0x00F8D648, a 16-bit length that counts the terminating zero and the string bytes, the icon as the tag byte at 0x00F8D654, the length 8 and the 7 digits of %07X, and 10 lines as the tag byte at 0x00F8D658, a 16-bit length and the line bytes. The three tag bytes read T, I and L. A byte of the writer record selects the byte order of the length.

It then formats the name mcr%d from the literal at 0x00F8D65C and the byte at B +0x0E through 0x00447620 and calls virtual slot 0x14 of the object behind B +0x04 with the dword at B +0x10, the formatted name, the name length plus 1 and 0. It calls slot 0x20 of the returned object, passes the buffer, its length and that result to 0x00D358D0, calls slot 0x24 of the returned object with 1 and calls slot 0x10 of the first object with the returned object, B and 0. What the slots do was not traced.

facts.claim: The callback tests the cell vector size before each of the two reads. Cell 0 is read as an int through 0x005819A0 and cell 1 as a Utf8String through 0x0071CE70. A failed size test calls 0x009D22B4.

The callback builds a visitor object through 0x00713AE0 from the value that ExecuteParameters +0x04 holds and the string. The object has the vftable 0x00FD5360, whose RTTI name is s_CharaIterateDisplayName. It stores the first dword of the value at +0x04, a copy of the string at +0x08 through 0x00447200 and 0 at +0x5C.

The callback calls 0x00764150 on W with the visitor. That routine takes the container at V +0x4E4 through 0x004D73A0 and calls virtual slot 1 of the visitor, 0x00718F40, with a pointer to each identity at node +0x0C until the visitor answers 0.

The visit method resolves the identity through 0x00CC7A50, casts the LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the CharaBase descriptor 0x012709A4 through 0x009DA6CC and answers 1 for a null cast. It requires the byte at control +0x5C to be nonzero, loads the record pointer at control +0x60 and requires the byte at record +0x59 to be nonzero. It compares the Utf8String at record +0x04 with the visitor string through 0x00445D20, which is true only for an equal length and equal bytes.
On equality the visit method stores the identity at visitor +0x5C and answers 0. Any other path answers 1. The walk therefore selects the first matching control in the key order of the container.

The callback tests the dword at visitor +0x5C. For a nonzero identity it loads Z = [Y +0x04], subtracts 1 from the cursor number and calls 0x0075B6C0 on Z with the cursor number and the address of the identity. A zero identity ends the native without a call. 0x0075B6C0 takes the target cursor state through 0x004D7310, resolves the identity through 0x004D9970 and, for a nonzero chara, calls 0x00562D30, the worker that builds the serverbound record 0x00CD with the second dword 0x18.
The callback destroys the visitor through 0x00713B60. It does not test the cursor number against the cursor count.

The meaning of the bytes at control +0x5C and record +0x59 was not traced. The visit method reads +0x59 through the pointer at control +0x60 without a null test, so a control with a nonzero +0x5C byte and a null record pointer dereferences the address 0x59. That case was not run.

rows.behavior: Reads a text command line, asks the text command parser object of the client to parse it and pushes 13 values. A failed parse pushes 13 nils. A successful parse pushes the command word, the count word, the counted dwords and the parsed strings, padded with nils to 13 and not capped at 13. It requests no yield.

pushes: int or nil for each counted dword, nil for a negative dword
Utf8String for each string of the vector
nil padding while fewer than 13 values were pushed

facts.claim: The registrar declares one Utf8String argument through 0x0072B5B0 and thirteen results through 0x00745380. Entries 0 and 1 are ints. Entries 2, 3 and 4 are Which<Utf8String, int> built by 0x0072C4C0 over the alternatives that 0x0072BD30 lists. Entries 5 to 12 are Utf8String.

The callback tests the cell vector size, reads cell 0 as a Utf8String through 0x0071CE70 and reaches W through R, X and Y. It calls 0x0075CCF0 on W with the string and the address of a local record. The routine loads V = [W], takes the parser object V +0x8BC through 0x004D7520 and jumps to the parser core 0x0056E380.

The local record holds a word at +0x00, a word at +0x02, three dwords at +0x04 and a vector of Utf8String values of 0x54 bytes at +0x10. The callback zeroes the vector fields before the call. The parser core writes the words at output +0x00 and +0x02 and passes output +0x10 to 0x0044E950 on one of its routes.
When the parser answers false the callback pushes 13 nils through 0x00748920.

When it answers true the callback pushes the signed word at record +0x00 and the unsigned word at record +0x02 as ints through 0x00584F70. It then pushes as many of the following dwords as the second word says. A negative dword pushes nil through 0x00748920 and any other dword pushes an int. It pushes each string of the Utf8String vector, stride 0x54, through 0x007487C0 and pads with nils until 13 values were pushed. Two routes of the parser core store 0xFFFF at output +0x00, which the callback pushes as the int -1.

13 is the padding target and not a cap. The callback sets a pad counter to 11 at 0x006FE375 and decrements it once per dword and once per string. It pads only while the counter is above 0 (0x006FE42C, jle at 0x006FE42E). Neither the dword loop, bounded by the second word, nor the string loop, bounded by the vector end, is capped, so more than 13 values are pushed when the second word plus the string count exceeds 11. A second word above 3 reads past the three dwords at record +0x04..+0x0F into the vector fields at record +0x10. The limits of the parser core were not traced.

facts.claim: The callback tests the cell vector size and the tag byte at cell +0x0C. A tag 6 cell, the Nil placeholder, keeps the default byte 5. Any other cell 0 is read as an int through 0x005819A0 and its low byte replaces the default.

The callback builds an empty Utf8String local through 0x00445CF0. It tests the tag byte at cell 1 +0x0C in the same way. A tag 6 cell keeps the empty string and any other cell is read as a Utf8String through 0x0071CE70 and assigned to the local through 0x00447450.
The callback reaches Y, copies the dwords [Y], [Y +0x10] and [Y +0x14] into a local through 0x0075D460 and calls 0x0075ED30 on the local with the byte and the string. 0x0075AF70 is a bare return.

0x0075ED30 loads W = [local], V = [W] and the object N = [V +0x174EC] through 0x004D7460. It returns without a record when N is null or when 1000 * [N +0x30C] + [N +0x310], taken as a 64-bit sum, is zero.

Otherwise it zeroes a 0x20 byte buffer, copies the first min(length, 0x20) bytes of the string into it when the first byte is nonzero and builds a record on the stack and passes its address to the sender 0x004D6D10 with two zero arguments. With s the stack pointer after the push of edi and the record base ecx = s + 0x20 (0x0075EE2C, after the two push 0 at 0x0075EE13 and 0x0075EE2A), the routine writes the dword 0xCF at record +0x00 and the dword 0x40 at +0x04, the low byte of the byte argument at +0x18, the low and high dwords of the 64-bit sum at +0x20 and +0x24, and the 32 byte buffer at +0x28..+0x47 as four consecutive qwords from the buffer at 0x0075EDF5, 0x0075EE04, 0x0075EE1B and 0x0075EE48. No instruction of the routine writes record +0x08..+0x17 or +0x19..+0x1F, so those bytes are uninitialized stack. The written extent ends at record +0x47, 0x48 bytes in all. A text of 32 or more bytes fills the buffer with no null terminator.
0x004D6D10 loads the same object N from V +0x174EC and tail jumps to 0x004E0240 for a nonzero N and answers false otherwise.

Reading the dword 0x40 at record +0x04 as a payload length, 0x08 header bytes plus 0x40 equals the written extent 0x48. The role is not stated by the bytes. xivl-opcodes:opcodes.json names the serverbound map opcode 0x00CF CountdownRequestPacket with the note no_pcap_evidence. The name is not established by a capture.

The unit of the 64-bit sum, the meaning of the byte argument, the role of the dword 0x40 and the effect of the default 5 were not traced. Whether an explicit nil passes the declared list was not run. No capture shows the record. Server behavior is unknown.
